name: Simple Analytics
description: Privacy-first / cookieless website analytics for agencies, enterprise teams, and white-label partners. GDPR + SOC 2 compliant, EU-owned, works alongside GA4. Freemium ("start for free"). Founded Aug 2018, NL. ~40.8k estimated users; 1,263 active subs.

mentions.evidence: ~$38,296 MRR, 1,263 active subscriptions, ~$40,283 L30, ~$1,893,017 all-time. Last sync Oct 4, 2026 ~04:07 Warsaw (02:07 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Own one privacy analytics wedge (cookieless + white-label for agencies, or EU-only hosting for regulated buyers). Sell the compliance story as hard as the charts.

whyItPrints: Analytics plumbing that marketing teams renew without thinking — especially when cookies and GA4 consent hell make privacy analytics a procurement checkbox. ~$38k MRR on volume seats; ~$1.9M all-time. EventDash-adjacent lane: "measure traffic without creepy tracking."
whyThisMatters:
Teams count pageviews, referrers, campaigns, and events without an analytics cookie. The IP address stays off the record, and a visit doesn't grow into a profile of that person. Setup is one script tag. An event can be a signup, a download, or a click off the site, and you can turn those into goals.

Lots of teams run it next to Google Analytics so they can compare the two counts. There's a free plan, a 14-day trial, and a longer proof of concept if a bigger team wants help with that comparison. Agencies report several client sites from one login. White-label puts the charts under the agency's own name. The company is EU-owned, hosts in the EU, and they talk about GDPR right next to the charts.

It doesn't record a session, build a cohort, or follow one person from a phone to a laptop. The company started in the Netherlands in August 2018.
